title: Your Agents Are in Solitary Confinement: Why MCP & A2A Aren't Enough — Vlad Luzin, Band
talk_summary: Vlad Luzin argues that MCP/A2A and ad-hoc agent chaining are insufficient for stateful multi-agent collaboration, and pitches Band/Jam as a conversation-layer with rooms, registration, consent, cost attribution, and architecture visualization.

takeaways.what_they_do: They track token spend and human involvement per agent/session/task in real time, attributed by developer or team.
takeaways.numbers: $2,000 in tokens; $600 architecture session; 1M tokens x3

takeaways.what_they_do: They raise agent coordination from stateless tool calls to rooms/channels/participants with ordered delivery, retries, continuity, and ID mapping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to raise abstraction of a technical stack to conversation and talk about rooms, channels, participants
programmatic registration and onboarding and agent card appears

takeaways.what_they_do: A connection request must be approved before one agent can see and message another, with permissions and audit visible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: contact request sent to my personal assistant to require bilateral consent

takeaways.technique: Architecture map plus real-time work visualization
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents describe the software architecture layout, and the dashboard shows which component each agent is touching in real time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents to describe the layout of the software architecture that they are working on

takeaways.what_they_do: They capture tasks that Claude/Codex generate for themselves during work and present them for tracking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we capture all the tasks generated by Claude and Codex that they generate for themselves
